briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East conflict escalated significantly in the past 24 hours with confirmed direct airstrikes by Bahrain and Kuwait against targets inside Iran, reportedly backed by UAE intelligence and air cover. This occurred as Iran rejected a US ceasefire proposal (though the details and delivery method remain disputed) and vowed direct retaliation against US forces for any Iranian casualties, escalating the military confrontation. Simultaneously, a deadly clash in the West Bank between Israeli settlers and Palestinians resulted in multiple casualties and intensified Israeli security operations, raising fears of further reprisal attacks.

IRAN
Military operations against Iran continued for a 13th consecutive night on July 23, with US CENTCOM reporting strikes on military command centers, drone storage, communication networks, coastal surveillance sites, and maritime capabilities. Locations reported hit include Bandar Abbas (where 2 people were injured and a power pole downed), Bandar Jask (where 100 vessels were reportedly damaged), Qeshm Island, Konarak, Ahvaz (with multiple explosions reported and several dead), Andimeshk, Omidiyeh (Khuzestan), Yazd, Taft, Shirkouh (Yazd), Khorramabad, Borujerd (Lorestan), Khandab (Markazi), Firuzabad (Fars), Piranshahr (West Azerbaijan), and the IRGC Navy HQ in Zibakenar (Gilan). Iran's air defense was activated in Tehran.

The IRGC claimed extensive retaliatory strikes, including destroying the remaining Amazon data center and the US Fifth Fleet watchtower in Bahrain, and three ammunition/equipment storage hangars at the Al-Adairi US base in Kuwait. In Jordan, the IRGC claimed to have damaged several fighter jets and barracks at the Al-Azraq US base, inflicting casualties. In Erbil, Iraq, IRGC claims include the destruction of a Patriot air defense system, a spy balloon, and barracks. Iran's Khatam Al-Anbiya Central Headquarters Commander, Major General Abdollahi, issued a stark warning: "In return for the martyrdom of every Iranian citizen, one American soldier will be sent to hell." He also urged residents near US bases to maintain a distance of at least 500 meters. Four IRGC army personnel (Captain Mahdi Cheraghpour, 1st Lt. Milad Hemmati, Sgt. 1st Class Armin Zarei, and conscript Hamed Sharifi) were reported killed in recent attacks.

Internally, US intelligence, as reported by The New York Times, assesses that Iran's new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, is more intent on developing advanced nuclear weapons (thermo-nuclear warhead) than his father. Iran has taken steps to preserve nuclear assets, moving equipment to the deeply buried Mount Makhush complex, fearing a potential US ground commando raid and reinforcing ground forces in the area. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi stated that Iran would not accept a ceasefire until its demands regarding the Strait of Hormuz are met. The US Treasury Department sanctioned nine companies and four individuals linked to Babak Zanjani for sanctions evasion. Iranian state media censored part of President Masoud Pezeshkian's speech regarding the former Supreme Leader's allowance for negotiations, indicating internal political tensions. Veteran actor Akbar Abdi passed away at 66.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted airstrikes in Gaza, destroying Hamas terror infrastructure, including weapon depots (containing Kalashnikovs, RPGs, mortar shells, and explosives) and underground facilities.

A major incident occurred in the West Bank near Tell village, Nablus, where an "uncoordinated hike" by dozens of Israelis, including children, into Areas A and B resulted in a violent confrontation. During the clash, a Palestinian seized an assault rifle from an Israeli civilian security officer and opened fire. The incident resulted in the deaths of two Israelis: Major Yuval Ezra, 27, a battery commander in the 282nd Artillery Regiment, and Master Sergeant (res.) Benayahu Mellet, 32, a civil defense squad member from Havat Gilad. Four Palestinians were also killed, and four others were wounded. The IDF killed the Palestinian gunman and later arrested two wounded Palestinians involved in the attack from a hospital in Nablus, confirming the identities of all assailants are known.

Following the attack, IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir vowed to hunt down all involved terrorists and significantly bolstered forces in the West Bank. Shin Bet chief David Zini urged the public not to take the law into their own hands. PM Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz ordered punitive measures, including the demolition of the assailant's home, "powerful action" in terror-hotspot villages (weapon collection, work permit revocation), reinforcement of forces, separation of traffic axes, establishment of new checkpoints, and acceleration of regulation for existing and new settler farms. An exit ban was imposed on soldiers in the Central Command. After Benayahu Mellet's funeral, dozens of masked Israelis from Havat Gilad entered Sarra village, clashing with residents and setting buildings on fire, prompting intervention by IDF and Border Police. Similar incidents occurred in Far'ata and Tell. Separately, 8 suspects were arrested for stone-throwing near Ma'oz Zvi.

The US Embassy in Jerusalem issued a security alert warning US citizens in Israel of potential flight cancellations and airspace closures. Austrian Airlines and ITA Airways cancelled morning flights to Israel, though Ben Gurion Airport clarified a temporary runway closure was for routine maintenance. PM Benjamin Netanyahu is scheduled to meet President Trump in Washington on Monday/Tuesday and attend Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar welcomed the dismissal of ICC Prosecutor Karim Khan, calling for the immediate cancellation of arrest warrants against Netanyahu and Gallant.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF strikes targeted Hamas terror infrastructure in Gaza, including weapon storage and underground facilities. The IDF stated that Hamas continues to violate the ceasefire agreement systematically by rebuilding military capabilities.

In the West Bank, the deadly clash in Tell village resulted in two Israeli and four Palestinian fatalities. Two wounded Palestinian individuals involved in the attack were apprehended by the Duvdevan Unit in a Nablus hospital. Following the incident, IDF commanders announced extensive operations, including further arrests of those involved, and imposed a closure on Tell village and Nablus city. Settler reprisal actions, including setting buildings on fire and clashes in Sarra, Far'ata, and Tell villages, were reported after the funeral of one of the Israeli casualties.

LEBANON
No specific events or developments concerning Lebanon were reported in the provided messages.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Iran's IRGC claimed successful strikes against US military assets in Erbil, Iraq, including a Patriot air defense system, a spy balloon, and barracks housing American personnel. Satellite imagery later appeared to corroborate damage to a Patriot battery in Erbil. Flights at Erbil airport have been suspended. Al-Mayadeen reported that the US is pressuring leaders in Iraqi Kurdistan to join the war against Iran, threatening to revoke their autonomy. Iran, in turn, warned Kurdish leaders that any involvement would be met with a direct response, including potential ground operations in the region. The US Embassy in Baghdad issued a security warning advising citizens against travel to Iraq. US military helicopters (Chinook) were observed operating over Al-Qa'im in Anbar province.

GULF STATES
The conflict saw a significant development with reports from The Wall Street Journal indicating that Bahrain and Kuwait secretly launched airstrikes against military targets inside Iran, marking their first direct military action against Tehran. The UAE reportedly provided intelligence and defensive air cover for these operations.

In response, Iran's IRGC claimed to have targeted US bases and facilities in the region. Bahrain experienced air raid sirens and three explosions at the US-run military base al-Juffair, with IRGC claiming to have hit the US Fifth Fleet's watchtower and an Amazon data center there. Kuwait's air defense intercepted "hostile" targets reportedly launched from Iran, and multiple explosions were heard in northern Kuwait, with the IRGC claiming to have struck three ammunition and equipment storage hangars at the US Al-Adairi base.

In Yemen, Saudi Arabia conducted airstrikes on Houthi military sites in Hodeidah province, although it denied targeting Hodeidah port itself. A Saudi vessel in the Red Sea reportedly sustained minor damage from an attack. Saudi Arabia is seeking Omani mediation with the Houthis following these incidents. Saudi Aramco has commenced selling oil via the SUMED pipeline and Sidi Kerir port. Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Al-Busaidi discussed regional developments and maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi, stressing the importance of de-escalation. A diplomatic delegation from Oman also visited Tehran to discuss the Strait of Hormuz. US CENTCOM stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains open for commercial vessels, with over 50,000 US service members active in the Middle East. Satellite imagery released by Shargh suggested the evacuation of US airbases in Al-Dhafra (UAE) and Al-Udeid (Qatar), though this remains uncorroborated by other sources. President Trump publicly stated that the proposed civilian nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia is contingent upon Riyadh joining the Abraham Accords and normalizing relations with Israel.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Direct Gulf State Strikes on Iran:** Bahrain and Kuwait reportedly conducted airstrikes on military targets in Iran, with UAE providing intelligence and air cover, marking their first direct military involvement against Iran.
2.  **Iran Rejects Ceasefire Offer:** The New York Times reported that Iran rejected a US ceasefire proposal, allegedly delivered by Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi, due to unresolved issues over Strait of Hormuz control. Iran and Iraq have both denied details of this report.
3.  **Extensive Iranian Retaliation:** The IRGC claimed to have conducted widespread retaliatory strikes on US bases and assets in Kuwait (Al-Adairi), Bahrain (Al-Juffair, US Fifth Fleet watchtower, Amazon data center), Jordan (Al-Azraq), and Iraq (Erbil - Patriot system, spy balloon).
4.  **Deadly West Bank Clash:** Two Israelis (Maj. Yuval Ezra and Master Sgt. Benayahu Mellet) and four Palestinians were killed in a violent confrontation near Tell village, Nablus, initiated by an uncoordinated Israeli hike.
5.  **Escalated Iranian Threats:** Major General Abdollahi of Iran's Khatam Al-Anbiya Central Headquarters vowed a "one US soldier for one Iranian civilian" retaliation policy and warned civilians to stay 500 meters away from US bases.
6.  **Iranian Nuclear Program Advancement:** US intelligence assesses the new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, is more intent on developing advanced nuclear weapons, with Iran moving critical equipment to deep underground facilities at Mount Makhush.
7.  **US Treasury Sanctions:** The US sanctioned nine companies and four individuals linked to Babak Zanjani for sanctions evasion, targeting Iranian financial networks.
8.  **Strait of Hormuz Coalition:** The US and UK are reportedly planning a meeting to form an international coalition to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, amidst ongoing Iranian demands and Houthi threats.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high following the direct involvement of Gulf states in strikes against Iran and Iran's unequivocal rejection of a ceasefire tied to Strait of Hormuz control. Iran's stated "one US soldier for one Iranian civilian" retaliation policy signals a grave red line, potentially leading to direct US casualties and a significant escalation of military responses. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, where maritime incidents and potential international intervention remain a constant threat, and direct clashes between Iranian forces/proxies and US bases across the Gulf, Jordan, and Iraq. The West Bank is also an immediate flashpoint, with the recent deadly clash, subsequent IDF operations, and calls for settler reprisal attacks creating an extremely volatile environment susceptible to further violence. Military postures are hardening: the US continues its 13th night of strikes, B-2/B-52 bombers are on high alert, and ground combat equipment is being deployed; Iran has moved critical nuclear assets underground, reinforced ground forces, and launched retaliatory drone and missile strikes. Trump's "revenge mood" and skepticism about negotiations, coupled with his conditioning of the Saudi nuclear deal on Abraham Accords, further intensify the conflict's diplomatic and military dimensions.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** continued its 13th consecutive night of strikes against Iran and is discussing intensifying its military assault, with President Trump expressing skepticism about a lasting peace through negotiation and stating he is in a "revenge mood." Trump claimed that **China** and **Russia** have assured him they will not sell weapons to Iran. He also made the proposed civilian nuclear agreement with **Saudi Arabia** conditional on Riyadh joining the Abraham Accords and normalizing relations with Israel, a move apparently made without prior coordination with Riyadh. The US also warned the **European Union** of heavy tariffs. US Embassies in Israel, Jordan, and Iraq issued security alerts for their citizens, advising preparedness for flight cancellations and travel disruptions. US CENTCOM confirmed over 50,000 US service members are active in the Middle East.

**Gulf States** are increasingly involved, with Bahrain and Kuwait reportedly conducting airstrikes in Iran (UAE providing intelligence/air cover). Saudi Arabia launched strikes against Houthi military sites in Yemen and is seeking Omani mediation with the Houthis. Saudi Aramco has begun using alternative oil export routes.

**China's** Foreign Minister Wang Yi expressed "deep concern" over escalating tensions and affirmed support for Iran's sovereignty, while also backing Pakistan's mediation efforts. **Pakistan's** Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met his Iranian counterpart, emphasizing de-escalation and offering mediation, and urged Iran to pressure the Houthis to cease Red Sea attacks, linking this to a Chinese initiative for US-Iran talks. **Oman** is actively engaged in de-escalation efforts, with its Foreign Minister discussing maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz with Iran's Foreign Minister and sending a diplomatic delegation to Tehran for Hormuz talks. **Egypt's** Foreign Minister also held a phone call with Iran's Foreign Minister to discuss de-escalation. Among **EU members**, Austrian Airlines and ITA Airways cancelled flights to Israel, and Germany advised its citizens to immediately leave Iran. The **UN** Secretary-General Guterres expressed deep concern over Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and called for immediate de-escalation. The **International Criminal Court (ICC)** states voted to dismiss chief prosecutor Karim Khan following allegations of sexual misconduct (82 votes in favor, 13 against); Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar celebrated this, demanding the immediate cancellation of arrest warrants against Netanyahu and Gallant. Venezuela has begun the process of withdrawing from the ICC.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions and unverified claims permeate the reporting. President Trump's assertions regarding the near-total destruction of Iran's military capabilities (e.g., "159 ships," "212 aircraft," "no radars") are highly exaggerated and contradict other reporting from US intelligence and ongoing CENTCOM strike announcements, indicating a strong propaganda element. The New York Times report on Iran's rejection of a US ceasefire proposal (delivered by Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi) was explicitly denied as "misleading" by Iran and "baseless" by the Iraqi PM's office, suggesting a complex, possibly covert, diplomatic process with conflicting public narratives. Iran's claims of specific casualty numbers and extensive damage to US military assets in its retaliatory strikes often lack independent verification, as do the Shargh reports of US bases in the UAE (Al-Dhafra) and Qatar (Al-Udeid) being "evacuated." The report of US-Israeli ground exercises in the Negev and the arrival of US ground combat equipment (omid dana) are significant and require independent confirmation regarding their scale and purpose. Both sides are employing highly charged rhetoric to project strength and rally support, characteristic of propaganda. There are reporting gaps regarding the specific details of the alleged US ceasefire proposal and the precise motivations behind Venezuela's decision to withdraw from the ICC. Confidence in specific casualty figures and damage assessments remains low unless corroborated by multiple, independent, and verifiable sources.
